meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Korea (Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act, Republic of Korea)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended; Articles 543 and 553-589 for Yuhan Hoesa); Act on the Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (FTRA, Act No. 5499, as amended, especially Articles 2, 5, 8-3 and 17); Enforcement Decree of the FTRA; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Articles 5-6); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Articles 11-15); FATF Recommendations. South Korea does not operate a public UBO register. Beneficial ownership is verified by Korean financial institutions and reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) as part of mandatory customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Chinese funding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation of the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notarization -> apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China or a provincial foreign affairs office under the Hague Apostille Convention (China acceded Nov 7, 2023) -> direct submission to Korean registry; no Korean consular legalization. For a document issued by a non-Hague state, the exclusive alternative is notarization -> local Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization -> legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in the issuing state. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Existence of the Chinese funding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation of the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notarization -> apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China or a provincial foreign affairs office -> direct submission to Korean registry. If the issuing authority belongs to a non-Hague state, use the separate consular route through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then the Korean Embassy/Consulate; do not add both apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing Korean incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chinese funding shareholder, notarized in the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notary -> PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or provincial foreign affairs office apostille -> use in Korea. Only if the issuing country is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention: notarize -> legalize by the issuing country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> legalize by the Consular Division of the Korean Embassy/Consulate. These two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Yuhan Hoesa Articles of Association (draft for registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant and Korean notary public under Commercial Act Article 543
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Korean original; notarized by a Korean notary public before filing with the Korean registration court. If the registered copy must be used abroad in a Hague state, obtain an apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; if the destination state is not an apostille member, obtain consular legalization from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the destination-state consulate. Never combine the two routes sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the Chinese funding shareholder (with branch seal and banker signature)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank certification -> PRC notarization -> apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China or a provincial foreign affairs office -> submit to Korean bank and registry. For a non-Hague issuing state, the exclusive alternative is bank certification -> local Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization -> Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of No Criminal Record for the resident director and central kitchen manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Security Bureau (for Chinese residents) or Korean National Police Agency (for Korean residents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued in the People's Republic of China: PRC notarization -> PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or provincial foreign affairs office apostille -> direct use in Korea. If issued in a non-Hague country: notarization -> local Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate. Do not use both apostille and consular legalization for the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening covers every beneficial owner at or above 25%, all directors, the resident manager, the master franchisee, the central kitchen manager, and every signatory. Screening must check the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, Korean sanctions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, KoFIU advisories and watchlists, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions if any US dollar clearing is contemplated, and EU/UK sanctions where relevant. PEPs, their family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence with documented source of wealth and source of funds. Banks will require continuous re-screening during account maintenance, adverse media checks, and identification of any round-trip capital red flags under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and China's outbound investment regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registration Information System (i-RO) at www.iros.go.kr, together with the National Tax Service HomeTax portal for subsequent business registration reporting
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be written in Korean characters under the Commercial Act and court publication rules. Romanized names are ancillary and do not constitute valid registration. For a bakery franchise, the recommended four-tier naming structure is: (1) geographic indicator such as Seoul or the target city; (2) the brand/trade name transliterated into Korean Hangul, avoiding Chinese script; (3) a business purpose descriptor such as bakery and food service; and (4) the mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa at the end. Any foreign-language brand name may appear in parentheses after the Korean transliteration but may not mislead or create proximity to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the competent High Court under Articles 110 and 113 of the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days, attaching the rejection notice, the proposed revised name, and the reasons why the rejected name is not identical, similar, or misleading. Before filing the appeal, the applicant can re-run the name search and submit a corrected proposed name through i-RO. The applicant may request one extension of the reservation before the 30-day window expires by filing a written request with the registration office; extension is discretionary and is granted only if no competing identical or similar name has been reserved and the applicant demonstrates justifiable cause.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected for the bakery license and for tax substance purposes in this industry. Under the Food Sanitation Act, a bakery restaurant classified under ISIC 5610 requires a physical store or central kitchen with actual food preparation, storage, drainage, water supply, and hygiene facilities; the local government health office conducts an on-site pre-licensing inspection before the food service business report is accepted. The National Tax Service also verifies the physical place of business for the corporate registration number and business registration certificate. A pure mailbox or PO Box address will be treated as lacking commercial substance and will be rejected by local authorities and by banks for corporate account opening. A serviced office with real meeting rooms, dedicated staff, and verifiable operational records may be acceptable only for the head-office address of the management company, but the bakery itself must have a physical commercial location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 75-85% probability of an unannounced or scheduled physical inspection within the first 12 months after opening. Checklist: (1) food hygiene and sanitation inspection by the si-gun-gu public health office under the Food Sanitation Act; (2) National Tax Service field visit to verify real business operations and place of business; (3) fire safety and kitchen ventilation inspection by the local fire department; (4) building code and zoning compliance inspection under the Building Act and National Land Planning and Utilization Act; (5) labor and employment standards inspection for pastry staff; (6) phytosanitary and customs inspection if Chinese-origin ingredients are warehoused in the central kitchen. All records, equipment, signage, and staff presence must be verifiable at the registered location.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea via the HomeTax System (www.hometax.go.kr) for VAT and corporate tax registration and electronic filing; Korea Customs Service (KCS) through UNI-PASS (www.unipass.kr) for export and import customs clearance and customs data exchange.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Korean Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), the representative director must file the Application for Business Registration with the competent district tax office or through the HomeTax System before commencing business. If the foreign investor has no domestic place of business for tax purposes, a domestic tax representative must be appointed under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Required documentation includes the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, constitutional documents of the foreign parent, board resolutions establishing the Korean entity, passport or proof of identity of the appointed representative, evidence of the Korean business address (lease agreement or utility bill), and proof of bank account opening. Upon approval, the NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number which is simultaneously the value-added tax identification number, corporate tax reference number, and employer withholding number for payroll taxes. The Business Registration Certificate is the primary evidence of VAT registration for issuing tax invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Commercial Act and Corporate Tax Act, taxed in its own name on worldwide income, with non-resident shareholders subject to Korean dividend withholding where applicable; no pass-through treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election; a Yuhan Hoesa is always treated as a taxable corporation under the Corporate Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch rules under Korean tax law apply to cross-border arrangements to prevent double non-taxation or deduction/no-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for registration; all persons supplying taxable goods or services in Korea are required to register under Article 5 of the Value-Added Tax Act. A simplified VAT compliance regime is available only to individual proprietors with prior-year annual turnover below KRW 80,000,000; corporations, including Yuhan Hoesa, are subject to the standard VAT registration and filing regime regardless of revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered businesses must issue tax invoices for taxable B2B supplies. Electronic Tax Invoice issuance through the National Tax Service HomeTax system is mandatory for taxpayers with prior-year annual turnover of at least KRW 100,000,000, and such electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS within one day after issuance. For businesses below this threshold, electronic taxation by approval is optional but must be implemented once the threshold is exceeded. Cash sales to consumers are substantiated through the NTS cash receipt system. The KCS and NTS exchange electronic customs declaration and VAT data in real time for cross-border transactions, forming an anti-fraud digital matching framework; exporters are expected to submit export data through UNI-PASS for automatic linkage to HomeTax.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, export of tangible goods is zero-rated where the goods are actually shipped out of Korea and an export declaration is accepted by the Korea Customs Service. Qualifying offshore services, including certain B2B digital services supplied to non-residents, are zero-rated when rendered to a foreign purchaser for use solely outside Korea and consideration is received in foreign currency from abroad. The zero rating is available only upon complete documentary substantiation showing the physical export or the offshore supply and the actual receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry) accepted and filed electronically through UNI-PASS by the Korea Customs Service
Commercial invoice issued by the Korean exporting entity
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment from Korea to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank-signed foreign exchange receipt/settlement certificate proving actual receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency from outside Korea
Foreign customer purchase order or executed international sales contract
Proof of business registration number and VAT tax invoice or zero-rated tax invoice records where applicable
Certified transport records or forwarder/customs broker reports evidencing export clearance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where export zero-rating is claimed but the required customs declaration, transport documentation, foreign exchange remittance evidence, or contract records are missing, unverified, or fraudulent, the NTS may disallow the zero rating and reassess VAT at the standard 10% rate plus interest. Additional tax penalties apply for negligent or intentional understating of taxable supplies under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. Repeated or fraudulent export zero-rating claims may subject the taxpayer to criminal penalties, aggravated fines, suspension of electronic tax invoice privileges, and retrospective clawback of VAT refunds. KCS may also impose separate customs penalties for false export declarations and the exporter may be placed under stricter customs inspection and trade compliance monitoring.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as policy authority; the BOK operates the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) and supervises authorised foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised current account regime for goods, services, and ordinary business income. The Korean won is freely convertible for settlement of trade and franchise royalty flows, but every transaction must be reported through an authorised foreign exchange bank using the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN). Current account items such as bakery ingredient imports, franchise royalty fees, and central kitchen equipment leases do not require prior ministerial approval or central bank surrender; the legal basis is the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Capital account flows, including inbound equity injection for the Yuhan Hoesa, require prior notification to the Korean authorities through KOTRA/FEIN, and the receiving bank reports the actual remittance to BOK/FEIN. There are no material restrictions on profit remittance if the company has complied with corporate tax filing and withholding obligations under the Korea-China tax treaty; however, banks may request evidence of underlying commercial substance to avoid suspicious transaction reporting. Export proceeds are not subject to forced conversion but must be credited within defined collection periods. Overall, Korea is a low-friction, high-reporting administrative convertibility jurisdiction rather than a strict licence-controlled foreign exchange system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, an exporter must collect export proceeds within six months from the date of export; extensions may be granted through the relevant domestic foreign exchange bank. No mandatory conversion ratio applies; 0% of export proceeds must be surrendered, but the foreign currency receivable must be receipted into a local domestic foreign exchange bank account and reported to BOK/FEIN using the applicable export purpose code. Failure to collect within the statutory period triggers a bank-led investigation and possible regulatory penalty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Proceeds Deposit) and KRW Corporate Operating Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Export Settlement Account
Franchise Royalty Collection Account and POS Settlement Account
Trade Settlement Account for Central Kitchen Ingredient Imports

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech digital banks and electronic money institutions cannot act as a primary local KRW treasury bank or hold customer deposits in South Korea. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act mandate that local currency deposit-taking, foreign exchange brokerage, and final settlement be performed by a bank licensed in Korea. Foreign EMIs may only provide payment-orchestration software or front-end invoicing over a licensed Korean bank's account; direct account onboarding for the Yuhan Hoesa is legally barred. Therefore, the treasury blueprint must use domestic Tier-1 Korean commercial banks for all KRW clearing, POS acquiring, and remittance rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the Yuhan Hoesa, statutory directors and the ultimate beneficial owner must complete an in-branch interview at the selected Korean commercial bank if they are Korean residents or non-residents with alien registration cards. Non-resident foreign directors may open the corporate account through a notarised power of attorney with Korean consular or apostille certification, but the bank will in practice require a recorded live video interview under domestic KYC rules. A purely remote account opening with no local agent and no interview is generally not accepted by Tier-1 banks for an operating company requiring POS and franchise royalty rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A foreign parent or Chinese master franchisor appears as the controlling shareholder, and the ownership chain is layered through multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate ownership chart from the ultimate individual to the Yuhan Hoesa; certificate of incorporation and current register for each non-Korean entity; source-of-funds evidence including audited financial statements, bank reference letters, and capital release vouchers; notarised and apostilled articles of association; sworn statement of identity and source of wealth from the ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive bakery POS revenue with fluctuating deposits and no traceable link to inventory, creating a potential money-laundering flag through daily cash deposits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed franchise agreements; monthly POS transaction logs reconciled to bank deposits; ingredient purchase invoices from approved central kitchen suppliers; inventory stocktake reports; National Tax Service filing acknowledgements; and a documented cash-handling policy with surprise audit provisions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Franchise royalty and central kitchen service fees remitted to an offshore parent or Chinese franchisor, raising transfer-pricing or trade-misinvoicing red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed franchise and master licence contract with a clear royalty formula; actual service evidence including delivery records, central kitchen production logs, and test reports; tax treaty residence certificates and withholding tax remittance statements; transfer pricing documentation with comparable benchmarking; bank confirmation that the royalty remittance is reported under the FEIN royalty purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered officers are non-resident foreigners without Korean tax identification and without demonstrable business presence in Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports and valid visas or alien registration cards; apostilled power of attorney if a Korean comptroller is appointed; National Tax Service business registration certificate; proof of lease or ownership of bakery premises or central kitchen; beneficial ownership declarations under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act; and personal credit and adverse-news screening results.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder should file a foreign investment notification with KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and obtain the Foreign Investment Notification Certificate. Capital funds are then transmitted by SWIFT MT103 from the overseas remitting bank to the Korean bank's capital escrow account using the FEIN foreign exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment in the acquisition of shares of a domestic Korean company. The Korean bank verifies the FEIN declaration, credits the proceeds to the escrow account, and releases funds into the operating KRW account only after the company completes capital verification with a Korean certified public accountant. All inbound funds must be reported to BOK/FEIN within the prescribed period, and the wire narrative should state that the transfer is a Korean-won capital remittance under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The Yuhan Hoesa will use SWIFT MT103 for franchise royalty, ingredient import, and service payments, accompanied by the appropriate FEIN purpose code and withholding tax clearance certificate. Local bakery POS revenues are cleared through a domestic acquiring bank; inventory payables and local central kitchen invoices are settled through real-time KRW interbank transfers. For large central kitchen equipment purchases from China, ICC UCP 600 letters of credit will be issued by the Korean bank and advised through the beneficiary's bank; documentary collections are handled under ICC URC 522. No outward remittance should be executed without the supporting tax invoice, commercial contract, and FEIN report to the foreign exchange bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts with a licensed Korean bank, limited to the Yuhan Hoesa's real trade or royalty exposure and supported by trade documents.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for onshore Korean residents are generally restricted; they are permissible only where a clear underlying trade exists and the bank has received BOK/FSC tolerance approval, and they should not be used as the primary hedging tool.
Cross-currency swaps for long-term central kitchen equipment debt, only under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and only for hedging, not speculation.
FX options and range-forward structures are allowed only to hedge existing current or capital account exposure and must be documented through the same FEIN reporting channel.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Meeting of Members and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Members (minutes physically retained at the registered office; no external filing fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year (for a 31 December fiscal year-end: by 30 June of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine; persistent failure to convene the meeting or to produce minutes is treated as an administrative irregularity. On creditor or member petition, the court may order dissolution of the company or impose compliance fines under the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Juridical Person Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of the following fiscal year; a one-month extension to 30 April is available when the company is subject to statutory audit and the audit report is not yet finalised
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax; under-reporting penalty of 10% (negligent) or 40% (intentional/reckless); daily delinquency interest of 0.022% accrues on unpaid tax until settled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: In practice filed together with the national return; generally due by 31 March (with the same one-month extension for audited entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional local income tax penalties equivalent to the national tax delinquency pattern, including surcharge rates up to 20% of unpaid local tax and daily late-payment interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory audit report (external audit result)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and finalised for submission to the members at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit report must be completed and presented before the annual general meeting; FSS registration must be made within one month after the audit report is finalised
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain or submit an audit report where required triggers administrative fines up to KRW 50 million under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; persistent violation may be referred to the prosecution and can lead to disqualification of directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registration of changes in constituted facts with the Registry of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in directors, registered officers, registered office address, or statement of contribution must be registered within 14 days of the effective date; there is no standalone annual re-registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed registration is punishable by administrative fines (not exceeding KRW 1 million) and may be lifted by the court; unregistered changes cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its delegated rules, a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint a qualified external auditor when (i) total assets at the prior fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12 billion; or (ii) it is designated as a public-interest-related company; or (iii) annual revenue exceeds KRW 20 billion and headcount exceeds 300; all thresholds are consolidated with any parent/domestic subsidiaries; once the threshold is crossed, the audit requirement remains applicable unless the company falls below the threshold for three consecutive fiscal years.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies above the statutory audit threshold; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP, SMEs standards) for smaller companies; all financial statements must be prepared in Korean won and reconciled to IFRS if required by the external auditor.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Republic of Korea does not operate a standalone annual UBO declaration form for a Yuhan Hoesa. Nevertheless, changes in member composition, contribution quotas, or directorships must be recorded in the relevant corporate registers and, where required by the Korean Commercial Act (e.g., amendment of the founding contract or reduction of capital), registered with the District Court registry within 14-30 days of effectiveness. In addition, any Korean bank account relationship triggers the reporting of beneficial ownership information under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and the Enhanced Due Diligence guidelines of the Financial Action Task Force, which must be updated whenever material ownership changes occur.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including contribution quotas, transfers and pledge rights)
Register of Registered Office and Founding Contract amendments
Register of Charges, Pledges and Encumbrances over members' quotas
Minute Book of the General Meetings and Board of Directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per full statutory audit for a mid-size bakery chain

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% for the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; 19% for the tranche between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion; plus a 10% local income tax surcharge, producing an effective statutory blended headline rate of 9.9%, 20.9% or 23.1% depending on the bracket.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No free-zone or tax-holiday exemption applies to a Yuhan Hoesa operating a specialty fresh bakery franchise and central kitchen in Korea; ordinary statutory incentives include the SME corporate tax special reduction, research and development tax credits, facility investment tax credit for automated bakery and kitchen equipment, job creation tax credit, wage increase credit, and temporary investment promotion credits; no patent box regime applies to bakery or pastry franchise royalty income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean National Tax Service (NTS) mandatory e-filing through HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) using the Corporate Tax Basis and Tax Return (Corporate Tax Return Form 1) together with supplementary schedules for financial statements, tax reconciliation, foreign related-party transactions, withholding reconciliation, and tax treaty reduction/exemption claims.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, based on the company's statutory fiscal year; a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa files once per fiscal year, with quarterly estimated corporate tax prepayments required for corporations meeting prescribed prior-year tax thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return and full payment must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal-year-end entity the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following year; an extension of up to one month may be allowed for external audit completion, but the tax payment deadline is not automatically extended and late-payment surcharges accrue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Identification and Resident Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Korean legal name, business registration number, representative director, tax office code, fiscal-year period, and corporate classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation and must file as a domestic corporation regardless of non-resident shareholding percentages; the filing itself does not change when the ultimate beneficial owner is a foreign individual or entity, but the non-resident shareholders must be disclosed in the withholding attachment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Gross Sales and Business Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare gross revenue from bakery retail sales, pastry counter sales, franchise initial fees, continuing franchise royalties, master franchise fees, central kitchen supply sales, and other ordinary business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Yuhan Hoesa receives royalty or supply income from a non-resident related franchisee, the full gross amount must be included in Korean taxable income before any deduction for cross-border expenses; if it pays non-resident related parties for imported Chinese pastry ingredients, the declared price and payment terms must satisfy the arm's-length standard and be reported in the transfer-pricing schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of Sales and Operating Expense Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report ingredient costs, direct bakery and central-kitchen labor, store rent, utilities, depreciation, advertising, franchise acquisition amortization, insurance, and operating overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties or technical fees paid by Yuhan Hoesa to a non-resident parent, licensor, or related brand company are deductible only if the expense is real, contractually supported, arm's-length, and subject to required withholding tax on the payment; if DTA paperwork is incomplete or the recipient lacks beneficial ownership, the payment is disallowed and may be recharacterized as a constructive dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Reconciliation of Book Income to Taxable Income and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting net income to corporate taxable income by adding non-deductible expenses, subtracting taxable-exempt income, adjusting provisions and reserves, and applying the available net operating loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss carryforward is limited to 5 years under the applicable filing framework; Yuhan Hoesa cannot use a loss year to shelter income if there has been a change in 50% or more of ownership plus a change in the real business and the NTS determines the loss was generated by tax avoidance; foreign-branch losses of other group entities cannot shelter Korean bakery-chain income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Corporate Income Tax Rate Calculation and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 9%, 19%, and 21% progressive corporate tax rates to the taxable income tax base, compute the 10% local income tax surcharge, and deduct applicable tax credits, including foreign tax credits and R&D/facility/job-creation credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Yuhan Hoesa is taxable on its worldwide income as a domestic corporation; non-resident shareholders cannot claim personal deductions or credits inside the corporation, and any foreign-source franchise royalty income earned by Yuhan Hoesa may claim a foreign tax credit only when foreign income taxes were actually paid and the treaty/credit filing requirements are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Withholding Reconciliation for Non-Resident Dividends, Interest, and Royalties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List each dividend, interest payment, royalty payment, technical-service fee, and other income paid or credited to a non-resident person; report the gross amount, statutory or treaty withholding rate, tax withheld, and net remittance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Yuhan Hoesa must withhold the statutory 22% effective rate (20% national plus 2% local surcharge) on outbound dividends and passive income unless a reduced DTA rate has been pre-approved; the withholding agent must file the monthly or quarterly Withholding Tax Return through HomeTax and attach the treaty application, Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and supporting contracts; failure to withhold creates personal liability for the representative director and a penalty equal to 20% of the withheld tax plus interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Foreign Related-Party Transaction Disclosure and Transfer-Pricing Adjustment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the international transaction schedule disclosing all cross-border transactions with related parties, including the counterparty country and entity, transaction type, amount, transfer-pricing method applied, and any year-end arm's-length adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The schedule must cover cross-border intercompany purchases, royalties, management fees, loans, and distribution arrangements; if Yuhan Hoesa uses a non-resident affiliate as a procurement hub for imported pastry ingredients and the price is not arm's-length, the NTS may impose an upward transfer-pricing adjustment, additional corporate tax, and a 20% unfaithful-return penalty; contemporaneous Local File and Master File must be prepared when statutory thresholds are exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Attached Financial Statements, Economic-Substance Evidence, and DTA Claim Exhibits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach the balance sheet, income statement, retained earnings statement, cash flow statement, notes, audit report if applicable, and any tax-treaty reduction claim package.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa, the NTS expects evidence of Korean economic substance: physical bakery/counter premises, central-kitchen equipment, employment records, lease agreements, franchise contracts, board resolutions, bank statements, and the non-resident beneficial owner's Tax Residency Certificate; without these exhibits the DTA claim is rejected and the entity may be treated as a conduit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or paying less than the correct tax triggers: (1) a non-filing negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; (2) an understated-return penalty of 10% of the understated tax where a return was filed but the tax base was materially underreported; (3) a late-payment additional tax of 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount; and (4) for intentional tax evasion, criminal referral under the Korean Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to 5 times the evaded tax; the NTS can also impose a travel ban/blacklisting on the corporation's directors and revoke business licenses.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on gross dividends paid to a non-resident plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax, making the total statutory effective dividend withholding tax rate 22%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a bilateral double-tax treaty, Yuhan Hoesa as paying company must, before remittance, collect and submit to the NTS through HomeTax: (1) the official application for tax treaty reduction/exemption; (2) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority in the year of payment, usually apostilled or bearing original signature, proving the recipient is a resident of the treaty country; (3) a beneficial-ownership statement confirming the recipient is not a nominee or conduit and has the right to use and enjoy the income; (4) board resolutions and commercial contracts showing the franchise/license loan is genuine; and (5) for royalty income, evidence of legal and beneficial ownership of the trademark, recipe, know-how, or other intellectual property. The reduced treaty rate is allowed at source only after proper filing; if the reduced rate is challenged, the withholding agent may pay the statutory 22% and the non-resident may file a refund claim within the statutory time limit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 22% (20% national plus 2% local surcharge), with common treaty rates of 10% to 15% for industrial royalties and technical fees, and reduced or zero rates for some cultural royalties; interest: statutory 22% (20% national plus 2% local surcharge), with typical treaty rates of 5% to 15% depending on the lender and beneficial ownership; if no treaty applies, the gross royalty or interest payment is subject to the full 22% withholding and no domestic deduction is allowed without proof that withholding was remitted.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in annual foreign related-party transaction amount triggers mandatory Local File preparation; KRW 100 billion in annual group revenue triggers Master File preparation; KRW 1 trillion of group consolidated revenue triggers Country-by-Country Report filing; even below these thresholds, Yuhan Hoesa must report all cross-border related-party transactions in the annual International Transaction Statement where the transaction amount exceeds the statutory disclosure threshold (commonly KRW 100 million per transaction type).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea is not a UAE-style ESR jurisdiction, but the NTS enforces a substance-over-form doctrine through Korean GAAR, the International Tax Adjustment Act, and the beneficial-ownership requirement in each DTA. Yuhan Hoesa must perform its Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Korea, including centralized bakery production, menu development, franchisee selection, store management, financial control, and significant economic risk-taking; if these activities are performed by a foreign affiliate while the Korean entity is merely a legal shell, the NTS can deny DTA relief, disallow intercompany deductions, reattribute income under the arm's-length rules, and apply the Korean controlled-foreign-corporation rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Corporate Income Tax Understatement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa operates dual POS systems to hide cash bakery and pastry counter sales, fails to record franchise initial fees, issues no receipts for cash purchases, and submits intentionally incomplete accounting records to the NTS, causing understated corporate income tax, VAT, and local income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korean Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3: imprisonment up to 5 years and/or a fine up to 5 times the evaded tax; the NTS will additionally impose a 20% non-filing/understatement penalty, late-payment interest at 0.03% per day, and a criminal referral for fraudulent tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced; the representative director and the accounting director are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and for civil restitution of the evaded amounts; the NTS imposes a travel ban and overseas travel restriction (blacklisting); criminal conviction results in imprisonment plus personal financial penalties, and the directors may be barred from serving as directors of any Korean company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Treaty Shopping, and Sham Royalty Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The ultimate non-resident owner forms an intermediary shell in Singapore or Hong Kong to invoice Yuhan Hoesa for fictitious Chinese-pastry recipe royalties and brand-management fees while no real employees, offices, marketing, or research activities exist in the shell, allowing the Korean entity to understate net profit and to claim a DTA-reduced withholding rate on non-genuine royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korean International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 3-2, 5, and 27 (anti-treaty-shopping, arm's-length adjustment, and controlled foreign corporation rules) authorize full disallowance of the sham royalty, upward adjustment of taxable income, denial of DTA benefits, and additional local income tax; the NTS imposes a 20% negligence penalty on the understated tax plus late-payment surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who approved the sham contracts is personally liable under Korean Commercial Act Article 401 for damages to the company and creditors; the NTS places the director on a travel-blacklist and freezes personal assets; criminal charges for tax fraud may be brought because the arrangement was a deliberate false declaration; directors may be personally assessed for the unpaid withholding tax on recharacterized dividends.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Foreign Exchange Violation, and Unlicensed Cross-Border Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Yuhan Hoesa receives master-franchise royalties and pays imported Chinese-pastry ingredient costs through unreported overseas personal accounts, cash couriers, or digital-asset exchanges, deliberately avoiding Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act declarations, financial statements, bank reporting, customs declarations, and suspicious transaction reports under the Financial Transaction Information Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act imposes fines up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment up to 3 years for unauthorized cross-border payments; customs authorities may impose additional customs duty plus evasion penalties on mispriced or undeclared imports of frozen pastry and flour; the Financial Services Commission/FIU can impose AML fines and criminal sanctions for failure to file suspicious transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director is personally criminally liable for foreign-exchange and AML violations; the FIU/NTS blacklists the director, imposing immigration holds and travel bans; the court may pierce the corporate veil because the LLC was used as an instrument for fraud, allowing personal asset attachment and civil restitution; the bakery and franchise licenses can be revoked, and franchisees may sue directors individually for losses caused by hidden liabilities.
